finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST parameter 'feed' is passed directly to file_get_contents(), which accepts URLs (http, https, ftp, php://, file://, etc.). An attacker can make the server fetch internal or cloud-metadata URLs (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) and read local files. The response only echoes the byte length, so exploitation is partly blind, but it still works as a port/host oracle and a request-forgery primitive. file:// and php:// wrappers also allow local file existence and size probing.

trace.note: Branch entered for any POST with 'feed' set; no require_admin() call
User-supplied value passed straight to file_get_contents (URL wrapper capable)
strlen of fetched body is echoed back, which gives a size/reachability oracle

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or host allowlist, no private IP or metadata blocking, no authentication. require_admin() is defined at line 4 but not called on this path. Session is started but not checked.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-12 passes $_POST['feed'] straight to file_get_contents() with no auth check (require_admin() at line 4 is only called at line 18 on a different branch), no scheme or host allowlist, and line 13 echoes strlen of the result.

finding.claim: SSRF via the set_webhook parameter: the user-supplied URL is passed to curl_init and curl_exec, so the server issues a request to any URL, including internal hosts and non-HTTP schemes (gopher://, file://, etc., since CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS is not restricted). Redirects are not followed (CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION not set), but the initial request is fully attacker-chosen. Gated behind an admin session, which lowers severity, but there is no destination validation.
finding.source: $_POST['set_webhook'] (authenticated admin user, or an attacker who has hijacked an admin session)
finding.sink: curl_exec($ch) at import.php:22 after curl_init($hook) at line 20

trace.note: Branch entered when set_webhook is present
curl_init($hook) sets the URL with no validation

finding.guards_checked: Admin session check only. No URL scheme or host allowlist, no private/link-local IP blocking, no CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction. The response is not returned, so the SSRF is blind.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() session check at import.php:4-9 (authorization gate only). There is no URL or host validation, so no guard closes the SSRF itself.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (import.php:17-22), but the sink at import.php:20-22 is reachable only after require_admin() at import.php:18 passes on $_SESSION['is_admin']. An unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker therefore cannot control the URL, and the source check treats an admin-only value as not attacker-controlled.
